description: Capybara Corps aim to integrate Mechanical, Aeronautical, Chemical, Biomedical, and Embedded systems engineering to complete the challenge chosen. We'll explore how these fields accompany each other in space and present it through the Junior Training game.
summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive space simulation game that allows players to learn through hands-on lunar missions. Players take on the role of an astronaut, performing essential tasks such as monitoring oxygen levels, managing water supplies, resolving system failures, and ensuring crew safety. The game recreates the challenges of living and working on the Moon, offering players a glimpse into the responsibilities of real astronauts.

Features such as oxygen shortages, unexpected emergencies, and decision-based consequences make the experience more immersive while teaching players the skills and responsibilities required for lunar exploration. Missions are intentionally designed to be simple and accessible, often requiring only basic interactions, making the game particularly suitable for younger audiences interested in science and space exploration.

What sets the game apart is its approach to education. Through contextual pop-up Knowledge Cards and informative hidden Easter eggs, players discover relevant scientific facts as they explore and progress through the game, making learning both engaging and enjoyable.
details:
Game Title – Lunar Recon

Story Line

The game starts off with a crew of four astronauts arriving on the surface of the moon in a space lander to an outpost that had already been built by autonomous robots long before the mission commenced. The player is one of the astronauts that have arrived on the moon and they get off the lander.

Oxygen, food, water, and radiation protection systems have not been activated by robots to conserve energy before the arrival of the astronauts so the player must first activate these systems through missions meant to guide the player through the game.

The game consists of 9 missions that the player must complete in order to win the game – the last one being the hardest: 30 days survival.

After the player has completed all 9 missions, the player will be able to watch a special MV which includes media about the game.

Purpose of the Game

The game aims to simulate how a lunar outpost would function in reality by portraying missions to be as realistic as possible. The game targets but is not limited to audiences aged 10-15, so anyone can also play the game and learn about space and moon exploration. For this reason, the game avoids extremely complex missions and usage of vocabulary to avoid confusion for the players. The game has also been specifically designed to be the furthest thing from boring. With interesting and fun features in our game, we hope to instill the idea that space exploration can still be fun and interesting rather than just another boring science topic.

Why play our game?

Most educational games fail to become popular among younger audiences because it looks and sounds like an educational game. We’ve specifically designed this game to look more like a regular yet interesting space exploration game while still being able to input the educational aspects. We had planned to implement NPCs that the player can interact with but the time limit caused us to hold off on that idea.

Usage of Tools


Game Engine & Development: Three.js, Postprocessing, Rapier Physics, Preact, Vite, TypeScript
3D Modeling Tools: Blender, gltfpack
Voice Generation: Kokoro TTS
Textures & Environments: Poly Haven (CC0)
Earth Imagery: NASA Blue Marble
Fonts & Typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, B612 Mono, Orbitron, Noto Sans Myanmar
Video Processing: FFmpeg
Testing & Compatibility: Playwright, Google Chrome

This project has been personally considered and thought thoroughly by the Game Director to maximize creativity with polishing and formatting being the only features that uses the help of AI. Every single team member has pitched their own ideas (such as the mirror and the Sun glare) but we could not implement every single feature. AI has not been used for the written part of this session (Project Detail) to retain originality.
